name: Question 9
worked_solution:
By the scalar function multiple rule, we have

$$
(u(t)g(t))^{′}=u(t){g}^{′}(t)+{u}^{′}(t)g(t).
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${g}^{′}(t).$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,2t⟩ \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-t) \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)g(t))^{′} & =u(t){g}^{′}(t)+{u}^{′}(t)g(t) \\  & =(1-t)⟨1,\,1,\,2t⟩-⟨t,\,1+t,\,{t}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨1-t,\,1-t,\,2t-2{t}^{2}⟩-⟨t,\,1+t,\,{t}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨1-2t,\,-2t,\,2t-3{t}^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Find (u(t)g(t))′ where g(t)=⟨t,1+t,t2⟩ and u(t)=1−t.

a
 ⟨1−2t,−2t,2t−3t2⟩
b
 ⟨t,−2t2,2t−3t2⟩
c
 ⟨1−2t,−1,2t−3t2⟩
d
 ⟨t−2,−t,t−2t2⟩
e
 ⟨1+t,2+t,t+3t2⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

By the scalar function multiple rule, we have (u(t)g(t))′=u(t)g′(t)+u′(t)g(t).

Let's find u′(t) and g′(t). g′(t)=⟨ddt(t),ddt(1+t),ddt(t2)⟩=⟨1,1,2t⟩u′(t)=ddt(1−t)=−1

Therefore, we obtain (u(t)g(t))′=u(t)g′(t)+u′(t)g(t)=(1−t)⟨1,1,2t⟩−⟨t,1+t,t2⟩=⟨1−t,1−t,2t−2t2⟩−⟨t,1+t,t2⟩=⟨1−2t,−2t,2t−3t2⟩.
